question:
A 37-year-old Hispanic female presents to the emergency department with a two-day history of
intermittent sharp and dull right lower quadrant pain. She reports no nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or
fever, stating she was asymptomatic before the sudden pain onset. The patient, who has no children,
confirms she is not pregnant. Physical examination reveals guarding on lower quadrant palpation.
Abdominal ultrasound shows free intestinal fluid and fluid in the gallbladder fossa. After evaluation, she
provides informed consent for a laparoscopic cholecystectomy. During the procedure, the surgeon
identifies an unexpected gastric mass with suspicious features of carcinoma. Regarding the newly
discovered gastric mass, what is the most appropriate next step? Answer Choices: (A) The surgeon
should proceed with biopsy under the emergency exception rule (B) The surgeon should complete the
cholecystectomy and not address the mass (C) The surgeon should document the finding and
schedule a separate procedure (D) The surgeon should proceed with biopsy since implied consent

covers incidental findings (E) The surgeon should consult the hospital ethics committee during surgery
(F) The surgeon should obtain consent to biopsy the mass from the patient when she wakes up from
cholecystectomy (G) The surgeon should contact the patient's next of kin for consent during surgery
(H) The surgeon should resect the gastric mass (I) The surgeon should biopsy the gastric mass (J) The
surgeon should obtain telephone consent from the patient's primary care physician
 A. The surgeon should contact the patient's next of kin for consent during surgery
B. The surgeon should document the finding and schedule a separate procedure
C. The surgeon should complete the cholecystectomy and not address the mass
D. The surgeon should resect the gastric mass
E. The surgeon should obtain consent to biopsy the mass from the patient when she wakes up from
cholecystectomy
F. The surgeon should biopsy the gastric mass
G. The surgeon should proceed with biopsy under the emergency exception rule
H. The surgeon should consult the hospital ethics committee during surgery
I. The surgeon should obtain telephone consent from the patient's primary care physician
J. The surgeon should proceed with biopsy since implied consent covers incidental findings
